Robin Richards

Nebraska Working People candidate for United States Senator, Nebraska · Challenger

Nonprofit consultant (executive director, Little Bird Consulting)

Robin Richards, 45, of Ralston is the Nebraska Working People Party nominee for U.S. Senate. She led the creation of the party, served as its first chair, and the Nebraska Secretary of State's Office confirmed her filing in September 2026. She sits on the Ralston Public Schools Board of Education, was the runner-up for Legislative District 12 in 2022, and ran as a Democratic write-in candidate for that seat in spring 2026.

Where Richards stands

Cost of living
Says her first priority is making life affordable. Supports wages that keep pace with living costs, plus accessible childcare, affordable healthcare and affordable housing.
Tariffs and trade
Says tariffs should be judged one at a time and used only when the benefit to industry outweighs the cost to producers and consumers. Proposes requiring House and Senate approval to extend a president's emergency tariffs.
Beef prices and agriculture
Says Congress should consider effects on Nebraska agriculture, including the risk of retaliation from other countries, before tariffs take effect.
Border security and immigration
Supports a secure border and an earned pathway to citizenship for long-term residents. Says enforcement should prioritize violent offenders. Opposes a blanket deportation approach that separates families or ignores due process.
Birthright citizenship
Opposes taking citizenship away from American-born children. Says Congress should instead fix the immigration system.
Taxes
Supports a fair tax system and child tax credits for families. Supports keeping Social Security benefits untaxed.
Social Security and Medicare
Says Social Security, Medicare, disability services and public education should be protected. Supports keeping Social Security solvent for today's workers.
Federal budget
Lists Social Security, Medicare, public education, veterans, infrastructure and public safety as her budget priorities. Calls for responsible budgeting and oversight of federal spending.
Party donor disclosure
Says the party will comply with every disclosure requirement in Nebraska law but will not voluntarily name the private donors who helped start it, citing the risk of harassment.

Background

  • Executive director, Little Bird Consulting (nonprofit consultant)
  • Member, Ralston Public Schools Board of Education, 2019 or 2020 to present; former board president, current treasurer
  • Founder and inaugural chair, Nebraska Working People Party
  • Candidate for Nebraska Legislature District 12, 2022 (lost to Merv Riepe)
  • Democratic write-in candidate for Legislative District 12, 2026 primary
  • Previously worked in finance and budgeting at a Nebraska state agency (per her 2022 Ballotpedia survey)
